issues.t: Windshield pillar trim can come loose in a crash
issues.sym: Usually nothing until a crash. Sometimes the trim on the pillar beside the windshield looks loose or rattles.
issues.why: A clip holding the pillar trim could be faulty on early-build cars, so the trim could come off when the side curtain airbag fires.
issues.next: Check the VIN for Audi safety recall 70D4 and have the clip inspected at your next visit.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner can fail
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds on cold start, a check engine light, misfires, or an engine that suddenly will not run.
issues.why: The tensioner that keeps the timing chain tight can let go, allowing the chain to jump. When that happens the valves and pistons can collide. A class settlement extended coverage on some of these years.
issues.next: If you hear a start-up rattle, stop driving and have the tensioner version checked. Replacing it early is far cheaper than an engine.

issues.t: Engine burns oil between changes
issues.sym: Low oil warnings well before the next service, needing to add oil regularly, and sometimes blue smoke or loss of power.
issues.why: The pistons and rings in this engine do not seal well enough, so oil gets past and is burned. Running low can damage the engine.
issues.next: Check the oil level every couple of fill-ups and have a dealer run a consumption test. Do not drive with the low oil warning on.

issues.t: Water pump and thermostat housing leak coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping, a sweet smell, pink crust or drips at the front of the engine, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The water pump and thermostat share a plastic housing that warps and seeps with heat and age.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed soon and keep the coolant topped up. Stop driving if the temperature warning comes on.

issues.t: Sunroof drains leak and can corrode an airbag inflator
issues.sym: Wet headliner or water in the front pillar and footwell after rain, and sometimes a sunroof that stops working.
issues.why: The sunroof drain setup can let water into the roof pillar, where it soaks foam around the side curtain airbag inflator. The inflator canister can rust and rupture.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 17V-001. Have any water leak fixed promptly and the inflator inspected.

issues.t: Front sunroof glass can crack in extreme cold
issues.sym: A loud bang followed by a cracked or shattered front sunroof panel in very cold weather.
issues.why: The glass panel on vehicles built from mid to late 2011 could break when temperatures are very low. Audi recalled them to fit a new panel.
issues.next: Check the VIN for Audi safety recall 60B2. If the glass is cracked, keep the shade closed and have it replaced soon.

issues.t: Electric coolant pump can overheat and catch fire
issues.sym: Often no warning. Possible burning smell or smoke from under the hood, even with the vehicle parked.
issues.why: The small electric coolant pump can jam with debris or short out from moisture and overheat. The first recall changed software and the second replaces the pump.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 17V-002 and 18V-229. If open, have them done now and park outside until then.

issues.t: Fuel pump flange can crack and leak
issues.sym: Fuel smell around the rear of the vehicle or inside, mostly with a full tank.
issues.why: The plastic flange on top of the in-tank fuel pump can develop fine cracks that let fuel seep out. The recall replaces cracked flanges and covers sound ones with a protective film.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V-660 and its 2017 expansion (Audi code 20Z8). Leaking fuel is a fire risk, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Auxiliary heater connector can corrode and melt
issues.sym: Burning plastic smell from the vents, reduced cabin heat, or in rare cases smoke.
issues.why: The connector for the electric auxiliary heater can corrode, heat up and melt nearby wiring.
issues.next: Check the VIN for Audi safety recall 80C5 / 80C6. If you smell burning, turn the climate system off and have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Seat-mounted side airbag inflator can rupture
issues.sym: No symptom before a crash. In a crash the side airbag in the seat may not protect properly.
issues.why: Inflators in the seat side airbags on vehicles built in early 2015 could burst when deploying.
issues.next: Check the VIN for Audi safety recall 69M1 and have the airbag modules replaced if it is open.

issues.t: Vehicle can roll away in Park
issues.sym: The vehicle creeps or rolls after being shifted to Park if the parking brake is not set.
issues.why: A fault inside the gearbox on a small number of 2017 vehicles can keep the parking lock from holding.
issues.next: Check the VIN for Audi safety recall 37K6. Always set the parking brake until the recall is confirmed done.

issues.t: Airbags and seat belt tensioners may not fire
issues.sym: Usually no warning, though an airbag light may be on. In a crash the airbags or belt tensioners may not work.
issues.why: Some igniters in the airbags and seat belt pretensioners on early-build 2018 vehicles may not trigger properly.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN for the open airbag recall and get the parts replaced before carrying passengers regularly.

issues.t: Valve cover bolts may be loose and leak oil
issues.sym: Oil smell, smoke from the engine bay or oil wetness around the top of the engine.
issues.why: The screws holding the cylinder head cover may not have been tightened correctly at the factory, so oil can escape onto hot parts.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-294. If you smell burning oil or see smoke, stop and have it inspected because of the fire risk.

issues.t: Air bag control unit can corrode and fail (recall)
issues.sym: An air bag warning light on the dash, sometimes coming and going.
issues.why: Moisture can reach the air bag control unit and corrode it until it no longer works.
issues.next: Have the control unit replaced under the recall; with it faulty the air bags may not fire in a crash.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can lose pressure (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal sinks or goes soft and the car takes much longer to stop.
issues.why: The master cylinder casting can be made too short, so the seals do not work as intended and pressure escapes.
issues.next: Have it replaced under the recall straight away; the electric parking brake still works, but normal braking can disappear with little warning.

issues.t: Wheel arch trim can work loose and fall off
issues.sym: Flapping or rattling from a wheel arch at speed, and a trim piece hanging away from the body or missing.
issues.why: The fasteners holding the wheel arch cover can let go, so the trim lifts in the airflow.
issues.next: Have the trim refastened under the recall at your convenience; a piece that comes off becomes a hazard for the car behind.

issues.t: Water can reach the gateway module and cut engine power
issues.sym: A sudden loss of drive power, many warning messages at once, or a car that goes dead and will not restart.
issues.why: Liquid can get to the gateway control module, the hub that passes messages between systems, and shut it down.
issues.next: Have the recall work done without delay and mention any damp carpet; losing power in traffic is a crash risk.

issues.t: Front brake caliper pistons may be badly coated (recall)
issues.sym: Weak braking or a pedal that needs more effort than it used to for the same stop.
issues.why: The caliper pistons may not have enough protective coating, so they corrode and stop moving freely.
issues.next: Do not drive until a dealer has checked the calipers under the recall; braking can be reduced without any warning light.

issues.t: Front seat backrest can break in a rear-end crash (recall)
issues.sym: The backrest may feel loose or move when leaned on, but often nothing shows until a crash.
issues.why: The seat frame and backrest adjuster may have been welded badly, so the backrest is not strong enough.
issues.next: Have the seat inspected and repaired under the recall; a backrest that folds back in a crash offers no protection.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm nut can corrode and break
issues.sym: The rear of the car feels unsettled or steers itself slightly, often with uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: The lock nut on the rear trailing arm can corrode until it breaks, letting the rear wheel move out of alignment.
issues.next: Have it replaced and the axle aligned under the recall soon; a loose rear arm can make the car hard to control.

issues.t: Rear axle alignment may never have been set (recall)
issues.sym: The rear tires wear unevenly, usually on one shoulder, far sooner than expected.
issues.why: After earlier repair work the rear axle alignment was not checked, so it can sit out of specification from new.
issues.next: Have the alignment checked under the recall and the tires looked at while it is on the rack; it is a wear issue, not a safety emergency.

issues.t: Reversing camera can show a blank screen (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays black or empty when reverse is selected instead of showing the view behind.
issues.why: A software fault keeps the camera picture from reaching the display.
issues.next: Have the software updated under the recall and look over your shoulder when reversing until then.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearings may be damaged from new (recall)
issues.sym: A deep knock from low in the engine that rises with revs, low oil pressure warnings, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: The connecting rod bearings can be damaged in build, so they wear quickly and lose their oil film.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the engine inspected under the recall if you hear knocking; a failed bearing destroys the engine and can leak oil onto hot parts.

issues.t: Rear seat belt retractors can lock too early (recall)
issues.sym: A rear belt locks up while being pulled out, making it hard to get a child seat tight.
issues.why: The retractor can go into its locking mode sooner than intended.
issues.next: Have the retractors replaced under the recall, and check any child seat is really tight in the meantime.

issues.t: Plug-in charging cable can overheat at the outlet
issues.sym: The plug, cable or household outlet gets hot, smells of hot plastic or shows scorch marks after charging.
issues.why: Charging at full current from a household outlet can overload the plug and the outlet it sits in.
issues.next: Stop using that cable and outlet and have it replaced under the recall; an overheating plug can start a house fire.

issues.t: High-voltage battery can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Hybrid system warnings, charging that stops on its own, or a hot or chemical smell from under the car.
issues.why: A fault inside the high-voltage battery can let it overheat, most likely while it is charging.
issues.next: Stop charging the car and have the battery inspected under the recall; the maker warns of a fire risk, so park it outdoors until then.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor connection can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: An air bag warning light, or the passenger air bag light saying it is off with an adult sitting there.
issues.why: The connection for the sensor that tells the car who is in the passenger seat can work loose.
issues.next: Have the connection repaired under the recall; with it loose the passenger air bag may not fire in a crash.

issues.t: Front seat belts may be built wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing shows in normal use; the belt latches and retracts as usual.
issues.why: The driver and front passenger belts may have been assembled incorrectly, so they may not hold an occupant in a crash.
issues.next: Have the belts replaced under the recall; there is no way to tell from the seat whether yours are affected.
